issues.legal_issue: The statutory power to take possession of and realize secured property following an industrial borrower’s default does not extend to property furnished by a surety.
material_facts: An industrial concern borrowed money and allegedly defaulted on its obligations.
Individuals furnished guarantees and provided their own properties as collateral security for the industrial concern’s borrowing.
The financial corporation directed that possession of the sureties’ properties be taken under its statutory recovery power.
issues.conclusion: The financial corporation could not proceed against the sureties’ properties under the power to take over and realize property of the defaulting industrial concern.
issues.legal_principle: Section 29(1) of the State Financial Corporations Act, 1951, authorizes action against the defaulting industrial concern and its property; it does not authorize taking possession of or realizing property belonging to a surety. The words “as well as” confer distinct rights exercisable against the same industrial concern. A surety’s liability may be coextensive with the principal debtor’s under Section 128 of the Indian Contract Act, subject to the parties’ contract, but that does not make the surety the defaulting industrial concern or extend the statutory power to the surety’s property. The statute must be read as a whole and strictly where it creates a special power that derogates from ordinary rights; an implied power cannot enlarge the persons against whom the statute authorizes action. The Court relied on the statutory text and structure, and on Reserve Bank of India v. Peerless General Finance and Investment Co. Ltd., Deewan Singh v. Rajendra Pd. Ardevi, Sarabjit Rick Singh v. Union of India, and Jamal Uddin Ahmad v. Abu Saleh Najmuddin.

predicates.appeal_against_quashing_recovery_action: The proceeding is an appeal challenging a decision that quashed recovery action against property furnished as security.
predicates.industrial_borrower_defaulted: The industrial borrower failed to meet its repayment or other contractual obligations.
predicates.secured_property_belongs_to_surety: A surety, rather than the industrial borrower, owns the property provided as security.
predicates.corporation_sought_possession_or_realiza: The financial corporation sought possession of or realization from the surety’s property using a power directed at recovery from the defaulting industrial borrower.
predicates.corporation_cannot_recover_surety_proper: The financial corporation cannot use the borrower-directed recovery power to recover against property belonging to the surety.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges recovery action against a surety’s property under a power directed at a defaulting industrial borrower, the corporation cannot use that power to recover from the surety’s property.

issues.legal_issue: A statutory application to enforce a surety’s liability is a separate, final recovery remedy and is not confined to seeking an interlocutory order or to cases involving a demand for immediate repayment.
material_facts: An industrial concern defaulted on its obligations to the financial corporation.
The sureties had undertaken liability for the industrial concern’s borrowing.
The statute provided a procedure for applying to a court to enforce a surety’s liability, including notice to the surety and an order enforcing liability if no cause was shown.
The financial corporation argued that the court-based remedy was available only for an interlocutory order or after a demand for immediate repayment.
issues.conclusion: The statutory application procedure provides an additional remedy to enforce a surety’s liability as a final relief; it is not limited to interlocutory relief or to a demand for immediate repayment.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 31(1)(aa), 31(1)(c), 32(1A), and 32(4A) of the State Financial Corporations Act, 1951, distinguish final relief enforcing a surety’s liability from the ad interim injunction available under Section 31(1)(c). Section 31 operates without prejudice to the other recovery remedies and permits an application upon the specified default, or where immediate repayment has been required and not made. The insertion of the surety-enforcement clause and its related procedure demonstrates that the remedy extends to sureties and is additional to the power directed at the industrial concern. The Court also relied on Delhi Financial Corporation v. Rajiv Anand, A.P. State Financial Corporation v. GAR Re-Rolling Mills, and the principle that statutory language must be given effect without supplying an omitted limitation.

predicates.proceeding_concerns_statutory_surety_enf: The proceeding concerns a financial corporation’s statutory application to enforce a surety’s liability for an industrial borrower’s debt.
predicates.industrial_borrower_defaulted: The industrial borrower failed to meet its repayment or other contractual obligations.
predicates.surety_is_liable_for_borrower_obligation: A person gave a guarantee or other undertaking making that person liable for the borrower’s obligation.
predicates.corporation_applies_for_enforcement_of_s: The financial corporation applied to a court for an order enforcing the surety’s liability.
predicates.surety_liability_may_be_enforced_as_fina: The court-based procedure may produce a final order enforcing the surety’s liability and is an additional recovery remedy.

issues.definition: Where a borrower defaults, a surety is liable, and the corporation applies for enforcement, the surety’s liability may be enforced as final additional relief.
